ui.gallery.title: 🔍 Gallery
ui.gallery.unlockHint: Complete the corresponding level to unlock
ui.gallery.char.shenmo.name: Shen Mo
ui.gallery.char.shenmo.title: Bookkeeper · Underground Operative
ui.gallery.char.shenmo.desc: Publicly a bookkeeper, secretly an underground intelligence agent. Skilled at passing messages through cage ciphers, calm and meticulous — the key courier of Operation "June Wind".
ui.gallery.char.vera.name: Vera
ui.gallery.char.vera.title: Old Bookshop Owner on Avenue Joffre · Liaison
ui.gallery.char.vera.desc: A White Russian refugee who fled to Shanghai with her family after the October Revolution, running an old bookshop on Avenue Joffre in the French Concession. On the surface a law-abiding foreign shopkeeper, in truth a key liaison of the intelligence network. She sets puzzles like traps — beneath her cool detachment burns a fervent conviction.
ui.gallery.char.suwan.name: Su Wan
ui.gallery.char.suwan.title: Bookkeeper's Wife · Guardian
ui.gallery.char.suwan.desc: Shen Mo's wife, guarding his small stronghold in silence. In these troubled times she wipes away the traces of his comings and goings, keeps a kerosene lamp lit for him by the stove, and sets out a bowl of warm rice porridge.
ui.gallery.char.ito.name: Ito
ui.gallery.char.ito.title: Tokkō · Confrontation over Evidence
ui.gallery.char.ito.desc: Ito of the Tokkō knew his father. He arrived ahead of time to verify the transmitter and left a completed puzzle in B3 — I've seen all your puzzles. This one, I finished.
ui.gallery.char.seal1.name: Star Balance Mark
ui.gallery.char.seal1.title: The Forty-Five Star Balance
ui.gallery.char.seal1.desc: A mark recording the law of the Star Balance, obtained after solving the library's puzzles.
ui.gallery.char.yamada.name: Yamada
ui.gallery.char.yamada.title: Tokkō · Senior Investigator
ui.gallery.char.yamada.desc: In Yamada's screening file, Shen Mo's name is annotated: Filing Category: Irrelevant. Two direction-finding vehicles lock down the library district from east and west, while Shen Mo counts a six-minute risk window in the dark.
ui.gallery.char.seal2.name: Three Generations' Marks
ui.gallery.char.seal2.title: Short Strokes and Vertical Lines
ui.gallery.char.seal2.desc: Shen Mo leaves short strokes, Ito leaves vertical lines, and his father left a deeper short stroke in B3 — three generations, three ways of carving, one and the same road.
ui.gallery.char.zhoutaitai.name: Mrs. Zhou
ui.gallery.char.zhoutaitai.title: 72 Dixwell Road · Guardian
ui.gallery.char.zhoutaitai.desc: Your father entrusted me with something before he left. He said — if he ever comes back, give this to him. The seal is intact, never opened.
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.1.name: Archive Fragment · I
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.1.title: Letter in the Rainy Night
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.1.desc: An unsigned letter, its seal bearing only a single hair-thin short stroke. Inside the envelope lies a fragmentary sudoku grid.
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.2.name: Archive Fragment · II
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.2.title: Trail of the Old Bookshop
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.2.desc: The old bookshop on Avenue Joffre is run by Vera, a White Russian liaison. She set a puzzle as the price of an audience.
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.3.name: Archive Fragment · III
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.3.title: Shadows in the Streets
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.3.desc: A mobile contact point emerges on Avenue Joffre, and Tokkō plainclothes agents linger. The web of surveillance has already begun to close.
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.4.name: Archive Fragment · IV
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.4.title: The Visitor Su Wan
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.4.desc: Su Wan recognizes this underground cipher and willingly covers your tracks. Yet the danger keeps rising.
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.5.name: Archive Fragment · V
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.5.title: The Library's Outer Wall
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.5.desc: The bricks at the corner have loosened, and a puzzle slip is wedged in the mortar. A hidden entrance surfaces — the hub of the entire cipher chain.
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.6.name: Archive Fragment · VI
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.6.title: The Brickwork Key
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.6.desc: Pushing the wall bricks by coordinates splits the wall open — the secret passage is now revealed, descending toward the library's lowest floor.
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.7.name: Archive Fragment · VII
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.7.title: First Steps into the Dark Stairs
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.7.desc: Water seeps from the stone walls, carved with broken sudoku remnants. Some old, some new, each from a different era.
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.8.name: Archive Fragment · VIII
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.8.title: Relics in the Hidden Chamber
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.8.desc: In a hidden stone chamber, Shen Mo finds a small brass key numbered 3, along with his father's handwriting.
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.9.name: Archive Fragment · IX
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.9.title: The First Closed Loop
ui.gallery.frag.ch1.9.desc: The letter, the old bookshop, the stone walls, his father's keepsakes... all converge here. All nine fragments of the prologue, unlocked.
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.1.name: Archive Fragment · I
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.1.title: The B1 Corridor
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.1.desc: The iron door swings open, and Shen Mo steps into the B1 corridor beneath the library. Both walls are covered with sequences of numbers carved by blade points, stretching toward the corridor's end — a long corridor of memory, countless puzzle fragments etched into stone.
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.2.name: Archive Fragment · II
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.2.title: Torn Note at the Fork
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.2.desc: The corridor splits in two midway, a half-rotted, crumbling page lying on the ground. Rule out the wrong fork and lock onto the main path — the identity of the 1938 fragment remains a mystery.
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.3.name: Archive Fragment · III
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.3.title: A Moment at the Bridge
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.3.desc: Shen Mo returns to the surface to resupply and passes the stone bridge outside the city. Deep in the bridge's shadow stands a middle-aged man in a grey cloth robe — friend or foe, surveillance has drawn close.
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.4.name: Archive Fragment · IV
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.4.title: The Old Residence at No. 72
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.4.desc: Following the trail to his father's former residence at No. 72, the courtyard long abandoned. A wooden cabinet stands open inside, holding his father's manuscripts and sudoku drafts.
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.5.name: Archive Fragment · V
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.5.title: Deciphering the Old Drafts
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.5.desc: Piles of sudoku drafts lie still inside the cabinet — some complete, some broken off halfway. His father knew every secret passage beneath the library, yet could never walk the final stretch.
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.6.name: Archive Fragment · VI
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.6.title: Return Underground
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.6.desc: The clues at the old residence exhausted, Shen Mo must return underground. The city grows more tense by the day, and Su Wan wipes away the traces of his absences at home, hiding the fact of his long disappearances.
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.7.name: Archive Fragment · VII
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.7.title: The Entrance to the B2 Stone Chamber
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.7.desc: Having walked the long B1 corridor, he reaches the heavy iron door leading to B2. The entire door is one enormous sudoku lock — and an unknown visitor arrived before Shen Mo.
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.8.name: Archive Fragment · VIII
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.8.title: The Empty B2 Chamber
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.8.desc: Stepping into the main B2 stone chamber, old wooden crates are piled in the corner and discarded manuscripts litter the floor. B3 truly exists but is sealed behind a chain of puzzles — an unknown visitor once lingered here.
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.9.name: Archive Fragment · IX
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.9.title: A Mark Left in the Chamber
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.9.desc: The marks of countless predecessors cover all four walls. Shen Mo takes out a charcoal stick and carves a mark of his own in a blank stretch of wall — no name, no date, only: I was here.
ui.gallery.frag.ch2.9.unlockedBy: Unlock after collecting all eight fragments of this chapter
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.1.name: Archive Fragment · I
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.1.title: The Hidden Door
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.1.desc: Shen Mo's gaze sweeps the inner frame of the hidden door — a fine pencil short stroke is carved into the wood, identical in style to the mark on the Avenue Joffre windowsill from the prologue.
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.2.name: Archive Fragment · II
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.2.title: The B1 Corridor
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.2.desc: The B1 corridor is cramped, its stone walls lined with endless carvings. The last three digits of the seventh mark match the note in the old coat's inner pocket exactly — the mud prints on the floor come from the Suzhou Creek bank, and a visitor passed here six hours ago.
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.3.name: Archive Fragment · III
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.3.title: The B2 Secret Chamber
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.3.desc: On the wooden table of the B2 secret chamber sits an open kraft-paper bag, seven sudoku puzzles laid out in order from easy to hard. On the topmost page, a line of pencil writing: You've arrived. This is the second layer the Teacher left.
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.4.name: Archive Fragment · IV
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.4.title: Seven Puzzles · One
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.4.desc: The first sudoku has few givens and a clean, crisp structure. At the bottom of the page, a line of small writing: Six more. No rush — you need the time.
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.5.name: Archive Fragment · V
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.5.title: Seven Puzzles · Two
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.5.desc: The second puzzle's complexity soars, cage lines interlacing layer upon layer, multiple cross-box cages entangling. The Teacher's hand: Do you remember that book from June? I set that puzzle. This one too.
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.6.name: Archive Fragment · VI
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.6.title: Seven Puzzles · Three
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.6.desc: The third is a zero-given sudoku — the entire grid holds only cage lines and sums, not a single pre-filled number. Shen Mo exhausts himself under the lamp before the deduction is finally complete.
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.7.name: Archive Fragment · VII
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.7.title: The B3 Entrance
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.7.desc: At the corridor's end stands a cast-iron door far heavier than any before it, a largely filled sudoku grid carved into its center — his father finished only two-thirds, and Ito arrived ahead to verify the transmitter.
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.8.name: Archive Fragment · VIII
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.8.title: The Transmitter
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.8.desc: At the deepest point of the stone chamber, an old transmitter rests on a wooden table, powered off. It bears signs of having been moved, the table leg carved with "3", and Ito completed his equipment inspection record.
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.8.unlockedBy: Unlock after collecting the first seven fragments of this chapter
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.9.name: Archive Fragment · IX
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.9.title: The Door at the Deepest Point
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.9.desc: At the chamber's deepest point stands a stone door a single person wide. Behind it, a tiny room holds only a table and a chair, with a tin box on the table. Inside the box, a single sheet of paper — the final third of the puzzle left blank at the B3 entrance by his father.
ui.gallery.frag.ch3.9.unlockedBy: Unlock after clearing the chapter's final level
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.1.name: Archive Fragment · I
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.1.title: 94 Dong Yuhang Road
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.1.desc: In the dusk, Shen Mo circles to the back alley of 94 Dong Yuhang Road. A freshly tied cotton thread is stretched in the mortar of the third utility pole, an old brass key with worn teeth tied to its end, the number 4 carved into the handle. A short stroke scratched by a fingernail on the inner door frame matches the mark he left outside the library's hidden door exactly — someone came before him.
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.2.name: Archive Fragment · II
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.2.title: Room 402
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.2.desc: In Room 402, an old exercise book lies open on the table, its pencil writing light yet resolute, four characters set down neatly: He hasn't come. It is his mother's handwriting. Below, a line of added small writing: I waited until November 15th. I can wait no longer. In the drawer, an old letter whose paper bears a sudoku puzzle — solve it, and you'll know where I am.
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.3.name: Archive Fragment · III
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.3.title: Room 403
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.3.desc: At the center of Room 403 stands an unlocked iron box, a note pasted inside its lid: Your mother solved half of this puzzle. The other half is left for you. Solved to the end, the final sequence of digits locks onto a crucial date — November 15, 1941, the day his mother left Shanghai for good. Beneath the box lies a scrap of newspaper from November 5, 1941: ten days earlier, the Japanese Imperial Conference had settled on the southward advance policy.
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.4.name: Archive Fragment · IV
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.4.title: Room 404
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.4.desc: An old photograph is pinned to the wall of Room 404 — a woman standing on a ship's gangplank, back straight, departing without looking back. On the back of the photo, a line in his mother's hand: November 15, 1941. I changed my ticket. Not Hong Kong. To Vladivostok. With the photo removed, a faint pencil line on the wall: You found this place.
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.5.name: Archive Fragment · V
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.5.title: Pan Hannian's Note
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.5.desc: In the mortar of the utility pole outside the back door of No. 94 is wedged a tiny, tightly folded slip of paper, dry to the touch — freshly placed. No signature, no date, only a single precise address: French Concession · Avenue Joffre · Lu Lu Tong Teahouse · Private Room, Second Floor. The folding is neat yet unpracticed — an entirely new, unknown hand.
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.6.name: Archive Fragment · VI
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.6.title: Lu Lu Tong Teahouse
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.6.desc: An old envelope rests on the table of the private room on the teahouse's second floor, its seal embossed with a fine nine-grid pattern, identical in origin to the anonymous letter that woke him in the prologue. Two sudoku puzzles sit side by side on the paper: solve the first, and use its key to solve the second. When both deductions conclude, the right-hand grid unlocks a new address and a precise time. And the teahouse has long been watched.
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.7.name: Archive Fragment · VII
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.7.title: The Other Road
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.7.desc: Vera's bookshop is shut tight, only an untitled old book lying flat on the street-side windowsill, its flyleaf in her hand: The road you walk is right. But there is another road. Wedged in the pages is a zero-given sudoku; when the solution concludes, a cold date surfaces — December 8, 1941. Faint words take shape: The next time you walk through this door, it will no longer be a bookshop.
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.8.name: Archive Fragment · VIII
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.8.title: The Backup Radio
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.8.desc: Beneath the desk in Room 404 hides a secret compartment, inside which lies a yellowed slip of paper, its creases worn by years: The backup radio is where you were last time. Beneath the library, B3, under the transmitter's base. The handwriting is unfamiliar, untraceable — the secret passage clues close into a loop, far beyond expectation.
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.8.unlockedBy: Unlock after collecting the first seven fragments of this chapter
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.9.name: Archive Fragment · IX
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.9.title: The Triple Alignment
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.9.desc: Late at night in the rain, Shen Mo returns to the B3 stone chamber beneath the library. From beneath the transmitter's base he removes a flat iron box holding a fully solved 9x9 sudoku, a line in Ito's hand at the bottom: I've seen all your puzzles. This one, I finished. His father's unfinished puzzle, his mother's trail, the Teacher's clues, Ito's completion — all paths now align in a triple convergence. In Yamada's screening file, his name is annotated: Filing Category: Irrelevant.
ui.gallery.frag.ch4.9.unlockedBy: Unlock after clearing the chapter's final level
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.1.name: Archive Fragment · I
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.1.title: Preparing the Transmitter
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.1.desc: Before dawn, Shen Mo returns to the B3 stone chamber. The power cord is connected, the dials remain at their initial calibration, and Ito's completed sudoku lies untouched in the iron box. The equipment is intact, awaiting only activation.
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.2.name: Archive Fragment · II
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.2.title: Power Down
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.2.desc: A low-frequency mechanical tremor persists overhead — the signature sound of a Japanese radio direction-finding vehicle, parked squarely above the library. Shen Mo sits motionless at the table, holding his breath. Now, there must be no sound at all.
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.3.name: Archive Fragment · III
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.3.title: The Direction-Finding Vehicle
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.3.desc: Rain shrouds the city. Shen Mo rigs a temporary directional antenna from the wire of an outdoor clothesline, dampening lateral signal radiation. Two direction-finding vehicles take position east and west, locking down the library district. He extinguishes the kerosene lamp and sits in total darkness, counting the six-minute risk window.
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.4.name: Archive Fragment · IV
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.4.title: The First Transmission
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.4.desc: The rustle of rain is the perfect transmission window. Shen Mo presses the key, sending in segments at three-second intervals, each burst no longer than five seconds. The first transmission completes in full, and no response signal returns from above.
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.5.name: Archive Fragment · V
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.5.title: The Second Transmission
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.5.desc: The second burst is shorter, yet it carries the core intelligence of the Pacific Fleet's coordinates. Just as the final character is about to be sent, footsteps suddenly close in overhead, stopping precisely near the hidden door below — a hair's breadth away, danger erupts.
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.6.name: Archive Fragment · VI
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.6.title: The Third Transmission
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.6.desc: Both earlier transmissions are out; there is no turning back. As the closing burst nears its end, three measured knocks sound overhead — someone knows he is transmitting. Shen Mo's mind stays steady as he sends the final intelligence character, then takes a neatly folded thin paper from his inner pocket and lays it gently on the transmitter's base: This paper is for the one meant to see it.
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.7.name: Archive Fragment · VII
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.7.title: Withdrawal Before Dawn
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.7.desc: With all intelligence sent, Shen Mo methodically finishes the cleanup — fully powering down the transmitter, unplugging the cord, retrieving the external antenna, restoring every trace of his operations. He retraces his route floor by floor, his pace calm and steady, leaving no sign of a hasty retreat.
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.7.unlockedBy: Unlock after collecting the first six fragments of this chapter
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.8.name: Archive Fragment · VIII
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.8.title: Yamada's File
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.8.desc: Shen Mo returns safely along the Suzhou Creek to the counting room, where Su Wan has long kept a kerosene lamp burning by the stove and quietly sets a bowl of hot porridge before him. He turns the white porcelain bowl on the windowsill, its rim facing due east, and presses a faint short stroke into the bowl's base with his fingertip. In Yamada's file, his name remains.
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.8.unlockedBy: Unlock after clearing the chapter's final level
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.9.name: Archive Fragment · IX
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.9.title: Daybreak
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.9.desc: A newsboy races through the wet stone alleyways, shouting at the top of his lungs: Extra! Extra! The Japanese navy has attacked Hawaii! America declares war on Japan! All three transmissions have landed, and the direction-finding team chased a false signal away — he slipped out through that window. Pearl Harbor erupts, and the Pacific war is fully ignited.
ui.gallery.frag.ch5.9.unlockedBy: Unlock after collecting all fragments of this chapter
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.1.name: Archive Fragment · I
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.1.title: The Counting Room
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.1.desc: Grey-white morning light spreads across the table, over the old ledgers and the antique abacus. Su Wan quietly stokes the fire to cook, speaking softly: Troop trucks passed this morning. Three. Heading west. Toward the Suzhou Creek bridge. In these troubled times, she guards his small stronghold in silence.
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.2.name: Archive Fragment · II
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.2.title: The Bookshop
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.2.desc: The old bookshop is shut tight, a neat short stroke carved on the inner threshold, identical to the mark he left in June. Wedged in the mortar of the third utility pole in the deserted back alley is a neatly folded note: The bookshop's puzzles have been destroyed. The remaining materials are where you first met. Someone, before him, took away the final step.
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.3.name: Archive Fragment · III
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.3.title: Bridge No. 4
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.3.desc: Beneath Bridge No. 4, a dark old coat rests on the stone steps, its cuff worn from long use. In the side pocket, an unsealed envelope holds a precise 1938 map of the Shanghai French Concession, the circled point marked in pencil not at the teahouse's current site but at the old address from before its 1939 move.
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.4.name: Archive Fragment · IV
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.4.title: The Old Lu Lu Tong Site
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.4.desc: The old Lu Lu Tong teahouse site stands empty. At the inner windowsill at the end of the ground floor, an iron box is bound crosswise with coarse cotton rope, knotted in the signature style of a familiar hand. On the topmost sheet inside: You've seen this map, which means you've reached the final step. This is the last original puzzle the Teacher left. She never finished sending it.
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.5.name: Archive Fragment · V
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.5.title: The Transmitter
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.5.desc: Late at night, Shen Mo returns once more to the library's depths. The transmitter's power cord has come loose, its cut clean and even — the mark of a precision tool. The tape sealing the base's iron box is intact, yet the box's edge has shifted slightly. This traceless power-down, this covert finish — it is Ito.
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.6.name: Archive Fragment · VI
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.6.title: The Marks
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.6.desc: In the dim B1 corridor, Shen Mo verifies from memory the number carvings covering the walls, confirming them intact. Then, fingers slightly bent, he draws a new short stroke beside the old ones — shorter and shallower than his father's. The mark on the hidden door's outer frame, the original carving at the B3 entrance... three points in one line, father and son of one blood. This web, he has finished it for his father.
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.7.name: Archive Fragment · VII
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.7.title: Yamada's Search
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.7.desc: In the early hours, the measured steps of a Japanese patrol halt abruptly at the alley mouth, hold for a moment, then move on along the alley — never entering the lane, never nearing the counting room. Su Wan speaks softly: Someone stood at the alley mouth for a while. Didn't come in. Ito, you already struck my name from that file late on the night of December 7th.
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.7.unlockedBy: Unlock after collecting the first six fragments of this chapter
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.8.name: Archive Fragment · VIII
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.8.title: Shen Shi'an's Traces
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.8.desc: In the third-floor study at 72 Dixwell Road, a fresh faint impression lies on the table — the base mark left by a thin old book resting there long. The hidden recess against the wall is deeper than before, bearing fresh signs of renewed use and pressing touch, yet the recess is empty. Father, before you left Shanghai, you came back to take the last thing. In early December, you arrived before me.
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.8.unlockedBy: Unlock after clearing the chapter's final level
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.9.name: Archive Fragment · IX
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.9.title: Pan Hannian
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.9.desc: In the private room on the second floor of Lu Lu Tong Teahouse, a man in a plain grey cloth robe sits waiting. Shen Mo spreads out the 1938 concession map; on its back, a line of pencil writing surfaces clearly: December 7, 1941. He is waiting for you. It was the same day he transmitted core intelligence deep in the night — his father left Shanghai, transited through Vladivostok, and made his way to Moscow. This web, at last, is fully woven.
ui.gallery.frag.ch6.9.unlockedBy: Unlock after collecting all fragments of this chapter
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.1.name: Archive Fragment · I
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.1.title: The Western Suburb Warehouse
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.1.desc: At the darkest hour of the night, Shen Mo steps out of Shanghai's city limits for the last time, standing in the shadow of the abandoned western suburb warehouse's outer wall. A large water-washed patch covers the center of the warehouse floor, erasing the area where the tin boxes once stood. At the bottom of the outer door frame, a fresh vertical mark is clearly visible — of the same origin as his April mark yet different in form, cut deeper and wider — the hand of another.
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.2.name: Archive Fragment · II
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.2.title: 72 Dixwell Road
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.2.desc: At daybreak, Shen Mo steps once more into the old house at 72 Dixwell Road. At the end of the ground-floor corridor, Mrs. Zhou stands long in silence, an old envelope with worn corners and yellowed paper open in her palm: Your father entrusted me with something before he left. He said — if he ever comes back, give this to him. The seal is intact, never opened.
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.3.name: Archive Fragment · III
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.3.title: The Avenue Joffre Old Bookshop
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.3.desc: The door of the Avenue Joffre old bookshop is sealed fast from the outside by a new iron lock. In the instant he turns to leave, Shen Mo catches in his peripheral vision a faint short stroke on the bookshelf board inside the windowsill — matching his June mark exactly, yet cut with the lightest touch, barely into the wood. In the very spot where he once took the hidden book, someone left the final destination pieced together over half a year — a clear pencil address.
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.4.name: Archive Fragment · IV
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.4.title: The Suzhou Creek
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.4.desc: In the afternoon the Suzhou Creek lies calm. Shen Mo sits quietly on the waterside steps and takes out the yellowed envelope. He opens it gently; on the smooth paper inside, a line of restrained writing: Mo — I am your father. I left, not because I didn't want to wait. The date is December 8th, the same day he completed his deep-night transmission of core intelligence.
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.5.name: Archive Fragment · V
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.5.title: Vladivostok
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.5.desc: Dawn light spills across the Huangpu River. Shen Mo reaches the dock before daybreak and walks to the end of the pier. At the window of the dock management office, he pays for a ticket without hesitation — the destination clearly marked: Vladivostok. It aligns perfectly with his father's evacuation route, the direction marked on the letter, and the sea route preserved in his mother's photograph. Three generations of hidden paths, converging at last on a single direction.
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.6.name: Archive Fragment · VI
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.6.title: The Counting Room
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.6.desc: A day later, Shen Mo returns to the counting room. Su Wan sits alone on the low stool by the stove; the white porcelain bowl on the windowsill faces due east — their silent ultimate signal of safety. She does not rise to ask, only lifts the pot lid and ladles out a bowl of warm rice porridge, setting it gently on the table. When do you leave. ...Tomorrow. Did you buy the ticket. ...I did. The porridge is warm.
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.7.name: Archive Fragment · VII
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.7.title: The Boat
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.7.desc: In the morning mist over the river, the ferry slowly weighs anchor, breaking free of the shore and gliding away from the Shanghai dock. Shen Mo stands at the rail — not holding it, not waving farewell, not looking back. In his inner pocket he carries all his past and his hopes: his father's letter, his mother's old photograph, the Teacher's original puzzle, the 1938 concession map. Shanghai is left behind.
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.7.unlockedBy: Unlock after collecting the first six fragments of this chapter
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.8.name: Archive Fragment · VIII
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.8.title: The Fog
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.8.desc: The ferry passes the mouth of Wusong, the river meeting the blue sea, sea fog rolling in layers. A long pale water trail stretches behind the stern, severing all ties with Shanghai. At the deck entrance behind him, someone pauses briefly, watching in silence — not approaching, not speaking, not leaving, hiding a trace of covert scrutiny. Coming and going without a trace, like all his past secret gambits.
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.9.name: Archive Fragment · IX
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.9.title: The Storeroom
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.9.desc: The sea fog lifts completely. Shen Mo sits in the cabin, spreading out one by one every object he carries. Footsteps sound behind him — one person, stopping three paces away. Ito: You walked it all. That vertical mark at the western warehouse was yours. You left short strokes, I left vertical lines. Your father's short stroke is in B3. Three generations. Three ways of carving. The key is left on the rail. The boat continues east. The horizon has no end.
ui.gallery.frag.ch7.9.unlockedBy: Unlock after clearing the chapter's final level
ui.gallery.prop.keyBrass3.name: Brass Key · No. 3
ui.gallery.prop.keyBrass3.title: His Father's Keepsake
ui.gallery.prop.keyBrass3.desc: In a dusty old wooden box in the hidden stone chamber, Shen Mo finds this small brass key, numbered 3, wrapped in yellowed silk paper. A few blurred lines of writing on the paper are in his father's hand — years ago, his father too had been here. Its purpose remains a mystery.
ui.gallery.prop.keyBrass3.unlockedBy: Clear Level 108 "Relics in the Hidden Chamber"
ui.gallery.prop.badgeAbacus.name: Badge · Star Balance Apprentice
ui.gallery.prop.badgeAbacus.title: Brass Abacus Bead Badge
ui.gallery.prop.badgeAbacus.desc: The entry credential of the Forty-Five Star Balance, its edge carved with a ring of fine abacus beads. It is the ticket to descend into the library's depths.
ui.gallery.prop.itoNotebook.name: Ito's Exercise Book
ui.gallery.prop.itoNotebook.title: Relic of the B2 Secret Chamber
ui.gallery.prop.itoNotebook.desc: An exercise book found in the iron cabinet of the library's B2 secret chamber, its pages covered with dense cage puzzles. Ito too once went deep into this place.
ui.gallery.prop.key4_94.name: Key · No. 4
ui.gallery.prop.key4_94.title: 94 Dong Yuhang Road
ui.gallery.prop.key4_94.desc: An old brass key with the number 4 carved into its handle, its teeth worn bright. It opens the door of 94 Dong Yuhang Road — the last door his mother left behind.
ui.gallery.prop.photoMother.name: His Mother's Old Photograph
ui.gallery.prop.photoMother.title: Room 404 · Departing Without Looking Back
ui.gallery.prop.photoMother.desc: An old photograph pinned to the wall of Room 404 — a woman standing on a ship's gangplank, back straight, departing without looking back. On the back, a line in his mother's hand: November 15, 1941. I changed my ticket. Not Hong Kong. To Vladivostok.
ui.gallery.prop.letterK734.name: The Teacher's Original Puzzle
ui.gallery.prop.letterK734.title: The Last Puzzle
ui.gallery.prop.letterK734.desc: The topmost sheet of paper in the iron box at the old Lu Lu Tong teahouse site: You've seen this map, which means you've reached the final step. This is the last original puzzle the Teacher left. She never finished sending it.
ui.gallery.prop.scrollSeven.name: His Father's Letter
ui.gallery.prop.scrollSeven.title: Suzhou Creek · Dated December 8
ui.gallery.prop.scrollSeven.desc: By the Suzhou Creek, Shen Mo sits quietly on the waterside steps and takes out the yellowed envelope. He opens it gently; on the smooth paper inside, a line of restrained writing: Mo — I am your father. I left, not because I didn't want to wait. Dated December 8th.
ui.gallery.prop.chartMother.name: His Mother's Route Chart
ui.gallery.prop.chartMother.title: Toward Vladivostok
ui.gallery.prop.chartMother.desc: The destination clearly marked on the ticket bought at the dock: Vladivostok. It aligns perfectly with his father's evacuation route, the direction marked on the letter, and the sea route preserved in his mother's photograph.
ui.gallery.inherit.coinVera.name: Vera's Coin
ui.gallery.inherit.coinVera.title: The Old Bookshop Pact
ui.gallery.inherit.coinVera.desc: An old coin Vera handed over, its edge worn. The token of the old bookshop pact.
ui.gallery.inherit.noteIto.name: Ito's Note
ui.gallery.inherit.noteIto.title: Traces of the Tokkō
ui.gallery.inherit.noteIto.desc: A note that fell from Ito, written in a hasty hand. Traces of the Tokkō.

ui.inkText.sentence.1: This book is not written for everyone.
ui.inkText.sentence.3: Father shut himself away not to write a book, but to hide something.
ui.inkText.sentence.4: Ito was the first to read these traces, and the only one.
ui.inkText.sentence.5: The bond between them is closer than you imagine.
ui.inkText.sentence.6: The day Father left, Ito began to leave vertical lines.
ui.inkText.sentence.7: You left short strokes, I left vertical lines — three generations, three ways of carving.
ui.inkText.sentence.8: You've read it all. But you haven't finished reading.
ui.inkText.sentence.9: Father did not vanish. He found another way to keep writing.
ui.inkText.sentence.10: Every vertical line Ito left is something Father wanted to say to himself.
ui.inkText.sentence.11: Three generations walked this road, but only one walked it to the end.
ui.inkText.sentence.13: You've read it all, but you haven't finished reading.
